question.:question/problem: If $\tan x = 11$, for some value of $x$, find the value of $\tan (x + 1π)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The period of $y=\tan x$ is $\pi .$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
\tan x=\tan (x+n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=1$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\tan x=\tan (x+1\cdot \pi )=\tan (x+1\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\tan x=11,$ we get that $\tan (x+1\pi )=11.$

generation.domain: x is any real angle at which tangent is defined; integer shifts preserve that domain
